ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that in rhombus ABCD, one interior angle $\angle BAD=80^\circ$, the diagonals AC and BD intersect at point O, and point E is on AB, with BE=BO. What is the measure of $\angle EOA$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
it follows that AC$\perp$BD, $\angle$BAO= $\frac{1}{2}\angle$BAD=$40^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle$ABO=$90^\circ$−$\angle$BAO=$50^\circ$,\\
since BE=BO,\\
it follows that $\angle$BOE= $\frac{180^\circ−\angle ABO}{2}$=$65^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$EOA=$\angle$AOB−$\angle$BOE=$90^\circ−65^\circ=\boxed{25^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, it follows that $AC\perp BD$ and $\angle BAO=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAD=40^\circ$. Hence $\angle ABO=90^\circ-\angle BAO=50^\circ$. Since $BE=BO$, it follows that $\angle BOE=\frac{180^\circ-\angle ABO}{2}=65^\circ$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, with A above, C below, B on the left, and D on the right; diagonal AC is approximately vertical and passes through A, O, C, and diagonal BD is approximately horizontal and passes through B, O, D; the two diagonals intersect at O; point E is located on side AB, and E and O are connected in the figure. Reasoning: The problem states that ABCD is a rhombus, ∠BAD=80°, and BE=BO. The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other, and diagonal AC bisects the vertex angle ∠BAD, so ∠BAO=80°/2=40°. Also because AC ⟂ BD, ∠AOB=90°. In right triangle ABO, ∠ABO=90°−40°=50°. Since E is on AB, ray BE is collinear with BA, so ∠EBO=∠ABO=50°. In triangle BEO, BE=BO, so the base angles ∠BEO and ∠BOE are equal, and ∠BOE=(180°−50°)/2=65°. Finally, ∠EOA is the remaining part of right angle ∠AOB after removing ∠BOE, so ∠EOA=90°−65°=25°.
